overview.headline: DNA sequencing reveals base order to explore genes and disease

keyPoints.point: DNA sequencing determines the order of bases in a DNA molecule and reveals genetic information.
keyPoints.quote: DNA sequencing determines the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyPoints.point: Adenine always pairs with thymine and cytosine always pairs with guanine in the double helix.
keyPoints.quote: Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T); cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G).

keyPoints.point: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs that hold instructions for building a human being.
keyPoints.quote: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs that spell out the instructions for making and maintaining a human being.

keyPoints.point: Nanopore sequencing involves threading single strands through tiny pores in a membrane to read bases one at a time.
keyPoints.quote: Nanopore-based DNA sequencing involves threading single DNA strands through extremely tiny pores in a membrane.
